cases.name: Victoria "Tori" Manisco
cases.about:
Her brother Tyler describes his sister as private and shy. Yet, Tori expressed herself in theater, blossoming on stage. She also spoke up for social justice issues, too. "Speaking up to people being harassed in public, racist speech, or misogynistic speech in public and she very passionate about that," he says. The siblings lived together, so she vocalized to him the troubles she faced taking the bus. "She took the bus to work since she didn't have a car and she was a decade-long user of public transportation. She was very proud of being knowledgeable of the system. She was very proud of that skill and that was used against her. On a daily basis, she was uncomfortable and made uncomfortable by men giving her attention that she didn't want; about negative attention based on her Asian race, based on her being a woman," he says. Tyler says she was followed and killed. "That basic invasion of her privacy, while she’s just trying to mind her own business in public, seems to be what got her killed. We don't know the specifics yet but it seems to be just her being a woman existing in public seems to but what caused her to lose her life and that's abominable," Tyler explains. Now, he's using his voice to advocate for his sister and other women facing violence. He adds, "What I want attention to is that we as men we don't consider that. That we'll be followed home on our way home from work, that we are unsafe on public transportation."

https://www.ksdk.com/article/news/crime/st-louis-brother-demands-change-after-sister-killed-in-string-of-shootings/63-cf2cb777-0e44-4659-993c-b22b64aaac78

Her obituary said, "Tori Manisco …..what words to use. Independent, actor, loyal friend, staunch supporter of Bernie Sanders, baby sister, precious daughter, creative, music lover, hyper-critical of her performances, beautiful vocalist, planner, politically aware and informed, profound writer, advocate for the down-trodden, fierce critic of idiots, skilled visual artist, socially introverted. Tori came into our lives at 6 months of age from an orphanage in Xiamen, China. She was tiny and sick, but a fighter and she persevered. She was a welcome and blessed addition to a family that wanted and needed her. She grew through a life of theater and performance that brought her to 2021 ready to fully blossom. At the age of 26, Tori was feeling that she was really coming into her own, at last. Her 26th birthday on April 2nd was joyous for her. She communicated at the time that she felt this was going to be her best year yet. On Tuesday August 10th, when returning from a rehearsal that gave her great joy, she was suddenly and violently taken from us. From her time at Crossroads College Prep (Class of 2013), to her degree work at Drury University, Tori did not make friends easily, but the friends she bonded with were precious to her and she guarded those friendships dearly. Since her graduation from Drury, Tori has spent time performing in local theater productions, working for Stages Performing Arts Center and Master Mind, and recently signed with Talent Plus Agency for commercial film and photography work."
cases.narrative: On 8/11/2021, she was found dead on the porch of her home on the 1100 block of Dover Place.

cases.name: Jean Kirk Kuczka
cases.about:
She was a health teacher at Central VPA High School in St. Louis, MO.

The 61-year-old teacher’s bio reads:

I cannot imagine myself in any other career but teaching. In high school, I taught swimming lessons at the YMCA. From that point on, I knew I wanted to be a teacher. I believe that every child is a unique human being and deserves a chance to learn. I also believe that Health is the most awesome subject in school, because, without your health, you cannot live to your fullest potential. I love teaching Health and Physical Education and guiding students to make wise decisions. Respect is my favorite word!

The teacher’s faculty bio says:

After earning her bachelor of science in education, she began teaching physical education at Seven Holy Founders in Affton, MO. For the next 16 years, Jean developed a physical education program for the K-8 SHF students. Wanting to teach strictly middle school children, Jean began her SLPS career at Carr Lane in 2002. At first, she taught physical education, but wanted to pass on her passion for health, so she developed a health program for the middle school.

After health became a state-required course for high school, Jean transferred to Central Visual and Performing Arts High School where she has taught Health, Personal Finance, and Physical Education since 2008.

According to the bio, she lived in Dittmer, Missouri, with her husband and one of her five children. “She enjoys spending time with her 7 grandchildren and is an avid bike rider,” the bio says. “Each year she participates in JDRF’s Ride to Cure to raise money to find a cure for juvenile diabetes, a disease her 29 year old son has been living with for 19 years.”

cases.name: Fannie Allred
cases.about:
For 30 years, she worked the halls of the Northwest Rehab Center where she served in the nursing field. Just this month, the 81-year-old had claimed her latest victory: defeating stage 2 colon cancer.

Her son Ronald Allred Jr. spoke to KSDK about his late mother.

“She was like the matriarch of the family actually,” he said. “She’s been in her neighborhood 20 plus years so everybody on the block know her, they looked out for her. Walking to and from the store, ‘Hey Ms. Allred.’ She’s just like, what they say, love.”

Her son Marvin Allred also spoke to the outlet, saying that Fannie was “one of the most beautiful souls that you would ever come in contact with.”

“It was nothing she wouldn’t do for you. This is like a dream/nightmare. Unfortunately, with her being so open hearted, it cost her her life,” Marvin added.

Fannie’s granddaughter Jermayor Allred also shared that she “was loved by everyone,” adding that many of the family members recently got together to celebrate Christmas.

cases.name: Lindsey Marie Smith
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Lindsey's life was marked by her constant optimism and determination to conquer challenges. She embraced each day with a positive outlook, believing in better days ahead. Her passion for life was evident in her many hobbies and interests. Throughout her career, she found fulfillment working as a Certified Nursing Assistant in helping the elderly and had a reputation for being a hard worker. She loved to clean, and found joy in planting, especially tulips. Lindsey had a fondness for Cardinal birds and all sorts of animals, which reflected her gentle spirit. She cherished memories with her family, particularly self-care nights spent with her daughter, Breanna. These evenings were filled with love, laughter, and creativity as they dyed Breanna's hair and applied face masks, creating lasting bonds that will forever be treasured."
cases.narrative:
On 1/19/2026, police were called to a home where a body had been discovered. Responding officers found a woman’s body on a metal door, which investigators believe might have been used for transport. 

Her remains were nearly frozen because of the cold weather, and blood had pooled under her head. She had reportedly begun to decompose prior to freezing. She had been shot in the head.

On 1/3/2026, Smith reportedly texted Ephron Tony Long she did not feel safe at his house and wanted him to drop her off where he had picked her up. No additional texts or calls were found on Smith’s phone after 1/3/2026. A witness reportedly heard a woman and man arguing in Long’s basement apartment followed by a single gunshot a few days before Smith’s body was found. Outside the home, investigators found blood spatter on the entryway and on the railing leading down to his door.
